title: Jason Cohen at MicroConf 2015: validating ideas, pricing up, product-market fit and staying fulfilled
summary: Jason Cohen answers bootstrapper questions on validating ideas by trying to invalidate them, getting paid upfront, raising prices aggressively, recognizing product-market fit, and why reseller distribution faded. He also live-coaches three founders on cash runway, finding new channels and marketplaces, and talks about motivation and stress.

principles.text: Validate by trying to invalidate: if feedback diverges after 'that's perfect,' the idea is weak.
principles.quote: the next person says that's perfect you know what you should do is take that and make it just for ad Tech and do that and someone else would say that's great you don't you should do is make that a freemium model

principles.text: Talk price in validation and take real payment up front; interest without a price is not validation.
principles.quote: it's important to talk about price because price does determine the product

principles.text: Raise prices far more than feels safe; test and keep doubling until signups drop.
principles.quote: what you gonna do next is double it again and feel that stops happening right

principles.text: Price to how customers buy: keep totals under the approval threshold so buyers need no permission.
principles.quote: if I spend less than five hundred dollars on my credit card I don't have to ask permission

principles.text: When small, raise existing customers' prices with an honest, personal note inviting them along on the journey.
principles.quote: honesty wins most of the time with most things of life including business

principles.text: Product-market fit shows up as sudden growth you can't fully explain, after a random walk of trying things.
principles.quote: you start growing faster all of a sudden and you look around say why and there's not really a great reason
